citation.sourceDocument: 26 U.S.C. §21 and §129, as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §§70404, 70405 (taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025)
citation.sourceNote: §21(a)(2): the applicable percentage is "50 percent— (A) reduced (but not below 35 percent) by 1 percentage point for each $2,000 or fraction thereof by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds $15,000, and (B) further reduced (but not below 20 percent) by 1 percentage point for each $2,000 ($4,000 in the case of a joint return) or fraction thereof by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds $75,000 ($150,000 in the case of a joint return)." §21(c): expenses of $3,000 for one qualifying individual, $6,000 for two or more, "reduced by the aggregate amount excludable from gross income under section 129". §21(d): no more than the lower earner's earned income, a full-time student or disabled spouse being deemed to earn $250 a month ($500 for two or more). §21(e)(2): a married taxpayer must file jointly. §129(a)(2)(A): a dependent care exclusion of up to "$7,500 ($3,750 in the case of a separate return by a married individual)", limited by §129(b) to the lower earner's earned income. Neither figure is indexed. State dependent care credits are not computed. Read on Cornell LII 2026-10-19.
